St. Thomas Cathedral in the Fort area is a truly beautiful place. The moment you step inside, the calmness hits you. The architecture is classic and elegant  : high ceilings, long pillars and detailed designs that make you slow down and appreciate the space.

Everything is well kept and peaceful and you can actually feel the history in the walls. It’s one of those spots in the busy Fort area where you can take a break, sit quietly for a few minutes and just breathe.

If you enjoy heritage buildings or are simply looking for a quiet and meaningful place to visit, this church is worth stopping by.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting St. Thomas Cathedral in Fort, Mumbai felt less like ticking off a heritage checklist and more like stepping into a quieter, more reflective version of the city—one that still breathes calmly despite the chaos outside. Tucked amidst the rush of office-goers, traffic signals, and colonial-era buildings, the cathedral stands with a grace that doesn’t demand attention, yet effortlessly commands respect.

What struck me first was the sense of calm the moment I entered the premises. The noise of Fort seemed to fade instantly, replaced by a soft stillness that felt almost therapeutic. It’s rare to find such a space in South Mumbai where time seems to slow down, inviting you to pause, observe, and simply be present. The cathedral isn’t just visually beautiful; it has an emotional weight to it—one that gently nudges you towards introspection.

The architecture is understated yet powerful. There’s no excessive ornamentation, but every element feels purposeful. The high ceilings, elegant arches, and stained-glass windows allow natural light to pour in, creating an atmosphere that feels warm and welcoming rather than intimidating. As sunlight filters through the glass, the interiors take on a soft glow, making it an ideal place to sit quietly, even if only for a few minutes.

What I appreciated most was how alive the space feels, despite its age. This isn’t a museum frozen in time; it’s a living landmark that continues to serve as a place of worship, community, and history. Reading the plaques and memorials, you’re reminded of the countless lives and stories that have passed through these walls—stories of colonial Bombay, changing times, and enduring faith.

St. Thomas Cathedral is not just for those interested in religion or history. It’s for anyone seeking a moment of calm, a connection to Mumbai’s layered past, or simply a peaceful corner to gather their thoughts. Every visit leaves you a little lighter, a little calmer, and with a renewed appreciation for the quieter, soulful side of the city.

featured_reviews.name: Foodieextreme Foodieextreme
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited July 15, 2025 – Day 12 in India

After visiting the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya museum, our guide brought us to St. Thomas Cathedral—a beautiful and deeply historic church nestled in the heart of Mumbai. Built in the early 1700s, it’s the city’s oldest Anglican church and feels like a peaceful sanctuary surrounded by history.

What took me by surprise were the many graves laid directly into the floor. I made sure my husband and our daughters, ages five and seven, were careful not to step on any. My girls noticed a small white grave and were curious if it belonged to a child. When we read the inscription, we saw that it was for a 54-year-old woman, the wife of an officer. That moment sparked quiet reflection and curiosity in all of us.

Inside, we saw the seat where Mother Teresa had once sat, which was marked with a small plaque. Nearby were two elegant seats once used by King George V and Queen Mary during their visit in 1911. My husband and daughters loved the experience of sitting in those very seats, imagining what it must have been like over a century ago.

What I personally loved most was the peace I felt in the church. Before this trip, many people had asked me to pray for them, knowing this journey was meaningful to me on a spiritual level. In the stillness of the cathedral, I took time to sit quietly and pray for each of them. It was a heartfelt and emotional experience.

We left with calm hearts and lasting memories. I truly loved this visit.

featured_reviews.name: ANIMESH SHUKLA
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Thomas’ Cathedral is one of Mumbai’s most historic and beautiful churches, offering a serene escape in the bustling Fort area. Built in 1718, it is the oldest Anglican church in Mumbai and an essential part of the city's colonial heritage. The church, now part of the Church of North India (C.N.I.), is not just a place of worship but also a significant historical monument.

Historical Importance: As Mumbai’s first Anglican church, St. Thomas’ Cathedral played a crucial role in the city's colonial past. It was built during British rule and remains a testament to the city's rich history.
Stunning Architecture: The church features classic Neo-Gothic and colonial architectural styles, with elegant arches, stained glass windows, and intricate carvings that transport you back in time.
Peaceful Ambience: Despite being in the heart of the bustling Fort area, the church’s interiors are calm and soothing, making it a perfect place for reflection and prayer.
Well-Preserved Memorials: The walls of the cathedral are adorned with memorial plaques dedicated to British soldiers and officers, offering a glimpse into Mumbai’s past.
UNESCO Recognition: The cathedral is a part of the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensemble of Mumbai, which has been recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Visiting Experience
Best Time to Visit: Morning hours are ideal for a quiet and spiritual experience. The church is open to visitors on most days.

Surroundings: Located near Horniman Circle, it is close to landmarks like Flora Fountain, Bombay High Court, Rajabai Clock Tower, and the Asiatic Library.

Mass Timings: If you wish to attend a service, check their schedule beforehand, as Sunday Mass is particularly special.

Photography: While photography is allowed in most areas, it’s best to be respectful as it is an active place of worship.

St. Thomas’ Cathedral is a must-visit for history buffs, architecture lovers, and anyone looking for a moment of peace in Mumbai’s fast-paced environment. Whether you admire its heritage, attend a service, or simply enjoy its quiet beauty, this cathedral is truly a hidden treasure in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text: Girgaon, formerly Girgaum, is an area in southern Mumbai in Maharashtra, India. Charni Road railway station serves Girgaon. The culture in Girgaon is diverse and varied. Like most areas of cosmopolitan Mumbai, residents span diverse languages, religions, traditions, festivals, and attire. Girgaon occupies prime residential real estate due to increasing demand just because of its prominent location in South Mumbai. The Sanskrit term "Giri" stands for hills, whereas the Sanskrit word "gram" denotes a village. Thus, Girgaon means a village at the foothill of mountains. A birds' eye view from the top of Malabar Hill will justify this etymological finding.

featured_reviews.name: Rakesh Singhavi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely shocking experience.

As a Jain family attending a function at Catholic Gymkhana, we were extremely disturbed by the condition of the venue. The first thing that struck us was the unpleasant foul odor lingering around the hall and kitchen areas. For a venue that regularly hosts weddings and family functions, the level of cleanliness and hygiene was appalling.

The kitchen and service areas appeared poorly maintained and unhygienic. The smell was so strong that many guests discussed it amongst themselves throughout the event. What was even more disturbing was the sight of rodents moving around near the food preparation and service areas. This raised serious concerns regarding food safety and sanitation standards.

The entire venue gave an impression of neglect and poor maintenance. Despite charging premium rates for functions, the management appears to pay little attention to basic cleanliness, hygiene, and guest comfort. Families expecting a clean and respectable environment for important occasions may be in for a rude shock.

I would strongly advise prospective clients to personally inspect the kitchen, service areas, and overall cleanliness of the premises before booking any function at this venue.This is strongly negative while remaining focused on personal observations and concerns rather than making factual claims that you may not be able to prove.

featured_reviews.name: Ameya Sapre
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a great time here with some catholic friends who are members of this place. Booze is cheap and food is damn good. The buff chilli was good and even the garlic bread and the chicken wings. Try out everything from their menu! Service is quick. Washrooms are clean. Definitely visiting again with the boys for a Friday nightout after work!

featured_reviews.name: Steven Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice Gymkhana for wedding and other functions. We attended a wedding function recently. The location of the Gym is bang opposite the marine drive promenade stretch near charni road. Valet parking was available.  The ambience was good. The washrooms were clean and we'll maintained. Along with the food and all other elements it turned out to be a good experience.

featured_reviews.name: Rakesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text: Food is excellent. We went there in hot summert 🌞 Temperature 43🫠. We were ask to wait for 20 min😓. But when food came all the waiting suddenly feel like worth it. 🤤

featured_reviews.name: Ashutosh Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely disappointing experience at Catholic Gymkhana.

The event was poorly managed, and there was absolutely no proper parking arrangement for guests. Many attendees faced unnecessary inconvenience just to find a parking space.

Another major issue is that the venue is located adjacent to a hospital. Even when only soft music was being played, police reportedly arrived due to complaints, disrupting the event and creating an uncomfortable atmosphere for guests. This is a significant limitation that prospective clients should be informed about in advance.

The entrance area was also unpleasant due to a foul smell coming from nearby garbage accumulation, creating a very poor first impression for guests arriving for the function.

What made the experience even worse was the attitude of the staff. The staff members were extremely rude, uncooperative, and irresponsible. They appeared least bothered about the inconvenience caused to guests and showed little interest in resolving issues or providing assistance when needed. Customer service and hospitality standards were far below what one would expect from a reputed venue.

Considering the cost of hosting an event here, the overall experience was highly unsatisfactory. I would not recommend Catholic Gymkhana for weddings, receptions, or other important family functions unless these issues are seriously addressed. ⭐☆☆☆☆

featured_reviews.name: Shalaka Salins
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been part of this church since childhood, and today as an adult, I can confidently say I have grown here—spiritually and personally. The people I’ve seen remain and thrive are those who truly seek God diligently through His Word.

This church has been a place of transformation in my life. I received salvation here, and my faith has deepened over the years. I also experienced healing from fibroids that I suffered from for years—something I truly believe is a blessing from God through faith and prayer.

From my day-to-day life to my education and life decisions, God has been with me through it all. Every guidance, every prayer I have received in this church, and the direction given through Pastor has played a significant role in making me stronger and victorious in my life.

The teachings here are rooted in the Word of God—nothing watered down to please ears, but truth that sometimes corrects and challenges. The Bible says, “Seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you,” and I have experienced this promise in my life.

Here, I was taught to read, meditate on, and follow the scriptures for myself. God is love, yes—but His Word is also a two-edged sword that refines and transforms us.

If you are someone who truly seeks God—not just comfort, but truth, growth, and a deeper walk in His light—this church is a place where you can experience that.

This is my testimony, and I continue to feel blessed beyond measure.

featured_reviews.name: Ramiah Daniels
featured_reviews.review_text:
My heart is filled with deep joy as I testify and rejoice at the great works of the Lord in my life through the Rose of Sharon Church, Kalina, Mumbai.
I have been a member of this blessed church since 1999, and my family and I have benefitted from the Word of God expounded by our Pastor Saroja M over the years. She is a mother to all members, even as a hen watches over her brood, praying constantly for our well-being and health and safety. Her counsel, when sought, is priceless, and it is only when one realises that this counsel is not of this world, but from the Spirit of the Lord, that one benefits from her advice and counsel.
A loving, caring, and disciplined Pastor, she will always teach us only as per the Holy Bible. When we receive her correction, it is a blessing, for it helps straighten our paths and keep us on our road to salvation.
Over the last 27 years, we have witnessed many personal miracles, blessings, and mighty deeds of our Lord Jesus in our lives and we owe a lot of this to our Pastor’s teaching, counsel, correction, and fellowship at the Rose of Sharon.

Specific miracles we have received from the Lord God through Pastor Saroja’s prayer over the years are many, but here are a couple
1)	In 2015, my dad’s LVEF Echo (Heart) parameters were at 20%. An LVEF of 20% indicates severe heart failure, specifically reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). It means the left ventricle pumps out only 20% of the blood filling it with each beat—far below the normal 50% - 70% range, signifying the heart cannot effectively supply enough oxygenated blood to the body. A Heart Surgeon I consulted told me to expect the worst and that any time, my dad could suffer a fatal attack. I tearfully called Pastor and she prayed for my dad. By the grace of God, dad is doing fine even today at 93, and in relatively good health, able to visit his church in Pune regularly! In fact, when we took the Dopple 2D Echo Test in 2020, his LVEF Echo (Heart) parameters showed 64%. Now, is that a miracle or what???
2)	In 2022, my mom had a brain stroke and was lying paralysed for over an hour at home. Finally, when help arrived and she was taken to hospital, I got to know and immediately called Pastor Saroja to ask for her prayers. Mom has recovered since and is able to even do work in the house and lead a relatively normal life, going to church regularly, even now at 91. Another miracle, showing us Lord Jesus’ mercy!

I thank Pastor from the bottom of my heart for all her support and prayers and for her constant encouragement in the Lord. May God bless her abundantly for all that she does for us, her flock!
Thank you Jesus!

Ramiah Daniels
Bangalore

Later on as he grew about 2 or 3 years old, he got piles, a small piece of flesh used to come out whenever he passed stool. But without consulting my Pastor I took him to doctor where I was given a long list of what he should not eat, that was almost nothing he can have and then l informed my Pastor regarding the same and she advised me to apply prayer oil and assured of her faithful prayers and within the period of 4 months  time he got completely healed as he is now 23 years old fit and healthy by God's Grace.

Now in the crucial year of 2004 I was pregnant for 2nd child where my husband didn't had job and as our Pastor had asked my sick father in law to stay in Rose of Sharon Ashram  in Mangalore who was suffering from lung cancer had come to Mumbai for his treatment and to live with us, and in mid of all chaos and fights in family my Pastor continually comforted me and my husband and assured us for her continuous pray for me to have a normal delivery, and as I got admitted to hospital for delivery the doctor told me that the child has not come down that's why she will have to go for C-section and assured me it is almost impossible to get second time normal because first time I had C-section and called for C-section doctor to come over for the operation, yet as my husband continually talking to my Pastor and she assured us for her faithful prayers, as I was going to the operation room for the last time the doctor wanted to check the baby and for her surprise the baby had come down and by God's Grace I had a normal delivery.

After my  2nd child on 2005 our life changed as per the Lord’s word spoken by our Pastor and her heartily prayers in that year my husband got job and we were blessed with our own house on October 2005 which our Pastor looked for us and not only that but also personally helped us to purchase biggest things to the smallest things which were needed for the new house.

After living happily with my family for 15 years in our new home, I was suddenly diagnosed with hereditary diabetes due to some carelessness, and my sugar level rose dangerously to 533. This led to a severe infection (pus) on the left side of my neck, requiring immediate surgery to prevent paralysis. During this critical time, I experienced God’s love through our Pastor, who constantly checked on my condition, stayed in touch with my family and doctors, and prayed for me sincerely. By God’s grace and her prayers, I was healed and given a new life.

A few years later, during COVID-19, I again faced a difficult time when I became the first woman in my area to test positive and was hospitalized along with my two children on separate floors, while my husband was abroad. It was an extremely painful and lonely experience, worsened by insensitive neighbors. Yet, through it all, I continued to witness God’s love and the unwavering faith, care, and guidance of His spiritual servant.

Through these trials, my faith has grown stronger. Like a plant nurtured over time, I have been spiritually guided, corrected, and blessed abundantly. I can never repay God, but I offer my heartfelt gratitude and praise to Him.
Praise the Lord.

featured_reviews.name: Cyrus Doodhmal
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Christmas Adventure at BKC

Our recent expedition from Colaba to BKC to celebrate Christmas with our dear friend Karen and the New City Church Mumbai congregation was nothing short of a festive adventure. The party, hosted at the chic WeWork BKC building on the 4th floor, was an absolute delight—once we finally made it there!

The journey itself felt like the pilot episode of a travel comedy. Picture this: navigating Mumbai’s unpredictable traffic, dodging potholes large enough to have their own postal code, all while enduring my better half’s running commentary on our cab driver’s “creative” driving techniques—and my increasingly desperate search for a restroom. Just when we thought we had escaped unscathed, the driver’s reckless decision to run a red light led to an impromptu street-side showdown with a couple of less-than-ethical traffic policemen. What followed was a dramatic scene featuring the foolish taxi driver attempting to bribe his way out, and me—the reluctant evangelist—on the verge of escalating matters if the bribe went through. Let’s just say this saga deserves its own blog post someday!

Thankfully, the evening that awaited us made all the chaos worthwhile. From the moment we arrived, we were greeted with warm smiles, infectious Christmas cheer, and Karen’s signature hospitality.

The vibe in the room felt like stepping into Bob Marley’s One Love—“Let’s get together and feel all right.” There was a beautiful harmony in the air, with cheerful carols, heartfelt conversations, and an unmistakable sense of joy and unity that wrapped around everyone present.

The setting struck a perfect balance of cozy yet vibrant. Special kudos to Pastor Anand, Karen, and the entire New City Church team for curating a celebration brimming with thoughtfulness and meaning. Every detail—from the festive decor to the uplifting interactions—made it an evening to treasure.

As for our ride back to Colaba? Let’s just say, by then, we had mastered the art of surrendering to Mumbai’s traffic chaos, leaving our fate in Santa’s trusty sleigh—or rather, the somewhat dependable hands of another cab driver.
